Period Drama · BBC · 2008–2011 · Complete Series

Lark Rise to Candleford

4 Series 40 Episodes Julia Sawalha 1890s Oxfordshire Based on Flora Thompson's Books

Adapted by Bill Gallagher from Flora Thompson's semi-autobiographical books, Lark Rise to Candleford follows young Laura Timmins as she leaves the hamlet of Lark Rise to work at the post office in the neighbouring market town of Candleford, under the eye of postmistress Dorcas Lane. Set in late-19th-century Oxfordshire, it ran for four series and 40 episodes on BBC One from 2008 to 2011. It streams on BritBox in the US. See how the services compare in British TV Hub's guide to where to watch British TV in the US.

What Makes the Series Special

Community

Two Communities, One Heart

The contrast between the poor farming hamlet of Lark Rise and the bustling market town of Candleford gives the series its gentle drama, and its real subject is how people look after one another.

At a Glance
PlacesLark Rise & Candleford
Character

Dorcas Lane

Julia Sawalha's Dorcas is generous, nosy, and fiercely independent, and her post office is the hub where every story begins.

At a Glance
RolePostmistress
A World Changing

The End of an Era

Set before the railway reached the area, the series quietly captures a rural way of life on the brink of change, which gives it a lovely, bittersweet warmth.

At a Glance
PeriodLate 19th century

Setting and Filming Locations

Setting & Filming

Oxfordshire Villages, Filmed in Wiltshire

The story is set in rural Oxfordshire at the end of the 19th century. The village sets were built and filmed around Box and Corsham in Wiltshire, with interiors shot in Yate, South Gloucestershire, and Chavenage House near Tetbury used for manor scenes.

At a Glance
SettingOxfordshire, 1890s
FilmedBox & Corsham, Wiltshire

Books Behind the Series

Source Books

Flora Thompson's Trilogy

The series is adapted from Flora Thompson's semi-autobiographical trilogy, Lark Rise, Over to Candleford, and Candleford Green, which draw on her own childhood in rural Oxfordshire and are usually published together as Lark Rise to Candleford.

At a Glance
AuthorFlora Thompson
BooksA trilogy

Frequently Asked Questions

Status

Is Lark Rise to Candleford finished?

Yes. The BBC ended the series in 2011 after four series and 40 episodes.

Quick Answer
StatusComplete
Ended2011
Streaming

Where can I watch Lark Rise to Candleford in the US?

Lark Rise to Candleford streams on BritBox in the US, including through the BritBox channel on Amazon Prime Video.

Quick Answer
PrimaryBritBox
Source

Is Lark Rise to Candleford a true story?

It's based on Flora Thompson's semi-autobiographical books, which draw on her own childhood in rural Oxfordshire, though the television series adds and expands many storylines.

Quick Answer
Based OnFlora Thompson's books
Viewing Order

Do I need to watch Lark Rise to Candleford in order?

Yes, it's best watched in order, since relationships and storylines develop across each series.

Quick Answer
In Order?Recommended
Cast

Is Brendan Coyle in Downton Abbey?

Yes. Brendan Coyle, who plays Robert Timmins, later played John Bates in Downton Abbey.

Quick Answer
Also InDownton Abbey
Filming Location

Where was Lark Rise to Candleford filmed?

The village sets were built and filmed around Box and Corsham in Wiltshire.

Quick Answer
CountyWiltshire
